title: Correct expression for x1
description: Essential: Student must derive and state the horizontal distance as x1(θ0) = 2z0 cot(θ0), identifying A=2z0 and b=1.

title: Application of Snell's law
description: Important: Student must correctly apply Snell's law (or equivalent ray equation) to deduce the circular ray path and relate the radius to z0 and θ0.

title: Energy density derivation
description: Essential: Student must derive and state the final energy density function ε(x) = 2Ez0 / (π(4z0² + x²)).

title: Energy conservation argument
description: Important: Student must use energy conservation, relating total energy E to the angular distribution and the derivative dθ0/dx.

title: Maximum distance x_max
description: Essential: Student must derive and state the final expression x_max = 2z0 cos²(θ0) / δθ0.

title: Overlap condition analysis
description: Important: Student must correctly set up the condition for the furthest point not reached, using the difference in x1 for nearby angles and the number of reflections.

title: Small-angle approximation use
description: Optional: Student may use a linear approximation (dx1/dθ0) for the small angular range δθ0.

title: Sign or derivative error
description: Pitfall: Student makes a sign error in the derivative dx1/dθ0 or misinterprets the absolute value in the energy density or overlap calculation.

title: Incorrect ray geometry
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly assumes a non-circular path or misidentifies the radius of curvature, leading to an incorrect x1.
